# gdu - go DiskUsage()

Pretty fast disk usage analyzer written in Go.

Gdu is intended primarily for SSD disks where it can fully utilize parallel processing.
However HDDs work as well, but the performance gain is not so huge.

## Installation

Head for the [releases page](https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases) and download the binary for your system.

Using curl:

    curl -L https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases/latest/download/gdu_linux_amd64.tgz | tar xz
    chmod +x gdu_linux_amd64
    mv gdu_linux_amd64 /usr/bin/gdu

Or you can use Gdu directly via Docker:

    docker run --rm --init --interactive --tty --privileged --volume /:/mnt/root ghcr.io/dundee/gdu /mnt/root

See [INSTALL.md](./INSTALL.md) for more installation options.

## Usage

```
  gdu [directory_to_scan] [flags]

Flags:
      --archive-browsing              Enable browsing of zip/jar archives
      --collapse-path                 Collapse single-child directory chains
      --config-file string            Read config from file (default is $HOME/.gdu.yaml)
  -D, --db string                     Store analysis in database (*.sqlite for SQLite, *.badger for BadgerDB)
      --depth int                     Show directory structure up to specified depth in non-interactive mode (0 means the flag is ignored)
      --enable-profiling              Enable collection of profiling data and provide it on http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/
  -E, --exclude-type strings          File types to exclude (e.g., --exclude-type yaml,json)
  -L, --follow-symlinks               Follow symlinks for files, i.e. show the size of the file to which symlink points to (symlinks to directories are not followed)
  -h, --help                          help for gdu
  -i, --ignore-dirs strings           Paths to ignore (separated by comma). Can be absolute or relative to current directory (default [/proc,/dev,/sys,/run])
  -I, --ignore-dirs-pattern strings   Path patterns to ignore (separated by comma)
  -X, --ignore-from string            Read path patterns to ignore from file
  -f, --input-file string             Import analysis from JSON file
  -l, --log-file string               Path to a logfile (default "/dev/null")
      --max-age string                Include files with mtime no older than DURATION (e.g., 7d, 2h30m, 1y2mo)
  -m, --max-cores int                 Set max cores that Gdu will use. 8 cores available (default 8)
      --min-age string                Include files with mtime at least DURATION old (e.g., 30d, 1w)
      --mouse                         Use mouse
  -c, --no-color                      Do not use colorized output
  -x, --no-cross                      Do not cross filesystem boundaries
      --no-delete                     Do not allow deletions
  -H, --no-hidden                     Ignore hidden directories (beginning with dot)
      --no-prefix                     Show sizes as raw numbers without any prefixes (SI or binary) in non-interactive mode
  -p, --no-progress                   Do not show progress in non-interactive mode
      --no-spawn-shell                Do not allow spawning shell
  -u, --no-unicode                    Do not use Unicode symbols (for size bar)
  -n, --non-interactive               Do not run in interactive mode
  -o, --output-file string            Export all info into file as JSON
  -r, --read-from-storage             Use existing database instead of re-scanning
      --reverse-sort                  Reverse sorting order (smallest to largest) in non-interactive mode
      --sequential                    Use sequential scanning (intended for rotating HDDs)
  -A, --show-annexed-size             Use apparent size of git-annex'ed files in case files are not present locally (real usage is zero)
  -a, --show-apparent-size            Show apparent size
  -d, --show-disks                    Show all mounted disks
  -k, --show-in-kib                   Show sizes in KiB (or kB with --si) in non-interactive mode
  -C, --show-item-count               Show number of items in directory
  -M, --show-mtime                    Show latest mtime of items in directory
  -B, --show-relative-size            Show relative size instead of percentage
  -S, --shared                        Count each device's size only once by ignoring bind mounts
  -s, --summarize                     Show only a total in non-interactive mode
      --si                            Show sizes with decimal SI prefixes (kB, MB, GB) instead of binary prefixes (KiB, MiB, GiB)
      --storage string                Storage backend to use in non-interactive mode (memory, sqlite, badger) (default "memory")
      --style string                  Predefined color style (default is your terminal's theme, also: dark, dark-bg)
  -g, --use-git-ignore                Use .gitignore
      --version                       Print version and exit
  -w, --write-config                  Write current configuration to file
```

      --min-age string                Include files with mtime at least DURATION old (e.g., 30d, 1w)
      --mouse                         Use mouse
  -c, --no-color                      Do not use colorized output
  -x, --no-cross                      Do not cross filesystem boundaries
      --no-delete                     Do not allow deletions
  -H, --no-hidden                     Ignore hidden directories (beginning with dot)
      --no-prefix                     Show sizes as raw numbers without any prefixes (SI or binary) in non-interactive mode
  -p, --no-progress                   Do not show progress in non-interactive mode
      --no-spawn-shell                Do not allow spawning shell
  -u, --no-unicode                    Do not use Unicode symbols (for size bar)
  -n, --non-interactive               Do not run in interactive mode
  -o, --output-file string            Export all info into file as JSON
  -r, --read-from-storage             Use existing database instead of re-scanning
      --reverse-sort                  Reverse sorting order (smallest to largest) in non-interactive mode
      --sequential                    Use sequential scanning (intended for rotating HDDs)
  -A, --show-annexed-size             Use apparent size of git-annex'ed files in case files are not present locally (real usage is zero)
  -a, --show-apparent-size            Show apparent size
  -d, --show-disks                    Show all mounted disks
  -k, --show-in-kib                   Show sizes in KiB (or kB with --si) in non-interactive mode
  -C, --show-item-count               Show number of items in directory
  -M, --show-mtime                    Show latest mtime of items in directory
  -B, --show-relative-size            Show relative size
      --si                            Show sizes with decimal SI prefixes (kB, MB, GB) instead of binary prefixes (KiB, MiB, GiB)
      --since string                  Include files with mtime >= WHEN. WHEN accepts RFC3339 timestamp (e.g., 2025-08-11T01:00:00-07:00) or date only YYYY-MM-DD (calendar-day compare; includes the whole day)
  -s, --summarize                     Show only a total in non-interactive mode
  -t, --top int                       Show only top X largest files in non-interactive mode
  -T, --type strings                  File types to include (e.g., --type yaml,json)
      --until string                  Include files with mtime <= WHEN. WHEN accepts RFC3339 timestamp or date only YYYY-MM-DD
  -v, --version                       Print version
      --write-config                  Write current configuration to file (default is $HOME/.gdu.yaml)
"""

def split_csv(v: str) -> List[str]:
    if v is None:
        return []
    res = []
    for part in str(v).split(','):
        part = part.strip()
        if part != '':
            res.append(part)
    return res


def parse_bool_value(v: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    if v is None:
        return True
    s = str(v).lower()
    if s in ('1', 't', 'true', 'y', 'yes'):
        return True
    if s in ('0', 'f', 'false', 'n', 'no'):
        return False
    # pflag would complain, but accepting odd values keeps behavior robust.
    return True


class CLIError(Exception):
    pass


def set_opt(opts: Options, attr: str, typ: str, val: Optional[str], original_flag: str):
    if typ == 'bool':
        setattr(opts, attr, parse_bool_value(val))
    elif typ == 'string':
        if val is None:
            raise CLIError(f"flag needs an argument: {original_flag}")
        setattr(opts, attr, val)
    elif typ == 'strings':
        if val is None:
            raise CLIError(f"flag needs an argument: {original_flag}")
        cur = getattr(opts, attr)
        # Command line string slice flags append comma-separated values.
        cur.extend(split_csv(val))
    elif typ == 'int':
        if val is None:
            raise CLIError(f"flag needs an argument: {original_flag}")
        vv = val
        if vv.startswith('='):
            vv = vv[1:]
        try:
            # Go's ParseInt accepts leading +/-, not whitespace for flag args normally.
            iv = int(vv, 10)
        except Exception:
            disp = INT_FLAG_DISPLAY.get(attr, original_flag)
            raise CLIError(f'invalid argument "{vv}" for "{disp}" flag: strconv.ParseInt: parsing "{vv}": invalid syntax')
        setattr(opts, attr, iv)


def prescan_config_file(argv: List[str]) -> str:
    default = os.path.join(os.environ.get('HOME', ''), '.gdu.yaml')
    i = 0
    stop = False
    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        if stop:
            i += 1; continue
        if a == '--':
            stop = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == '--config-file':
            if i + 1 < len(argv):
                return argv[i+1]
        elif a.startswith('--config-file='):
            return a.split('=', 1)[1]
        i += 1
    return default


def parse_args(argv: List[str], opts: Options) -> Tuple[Options, List[str]]:
    positionals: List[str] = []
    i = 0
    stop_flags = False
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if stop_flags:
            positionals.append(arg)
            i += 1
            continue
        if arg == '--':
            stop_flags = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if arg.startswith('--') and arg != '--':
            nameval = arg[2:]
            if '=' in nameval:
                name, val = nameval.split('=', 1)
            else:
                name, val = nameval, None
            if name not in LONG_FLAGS:
                raise CLIError(f"unknown flag: --{name}")
            attr, typ = LONG_FLAGS[name]
            if typ == 'bool':
                set_opt(opts, attr, typ, val, f'--{name}')
            else:
                if val is None:
                    if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                        raise CLIError(f"flag needs an argument: --{name}")
                    i += 1
                    val = argv[i]
                set_opt(opts, attr, typ, val, f'--{name}')
            i += 1
            continue
        if arg.startswith('-') and arg != '-':
            chars = arg[1:]
            j = 0
            while j < len(chars):
                ch = chars[j]
                if ch == '=':
                    # This only occurs after bool shorthands such as -np=false; ignore rest.
                    break
                if ch not in SHORT_FLAGS:
                    raise CLIError(f"unknown shorthand flag: '{ch}' in -{chars}")
                attr, typ, lname = SHORT_FLAGS[ch]
                if typ == 'bool':
                    # pflag allows -x=false when this is the last shorthand.
                    if j + 1 < len(chars) and chars[j+1] == '=':
                        set_opt(opts, attr, typ, chars[j+2:], f"'{ch}' in -{chars}")
                        j = len(chars)
                    else:
                        set_opt(opts, attr, typ, None, f"'{ch}' in -{chars}")
                        j += 1
                    continue
                else:
                    # The remainder of this token, if any, is the value; an initial '=' is stripped for ints/strings.
                    if j + 1 < len(chars):
                        val = chars[j+1:]
                        if val.startswith('='):
                            val = val[1:]
                    else:
                        if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                            raise CLIError(f"flag needs an argument: '{ch}' in -{chars}")
                        i += 1
                        val = argv[i]
                    set_opt(opts, attr, typ, val, f"'{ch}' in -{chars}")
                    j = len(chars)
            i += 1
            continue
        positionals.append(arg)
        i += 1
    if len(positionals) > 1:
        raise CLIError(f"accepts at most 1 arg(s), received {len(positionals)}")
    return opts, positionals


def apply_config(opts: Options, path: str):
    opts.config_file = path
    try:
        with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
    except Exception:
        return
    key = None
    list_acc = None
    data = {}
    def finish_list():
        nonlocal key, list_acc
        if key is not None and list_acc is not None:
            data[key] = list_acc
        key = None; list_acc = None
    for raw in lines:
        line = raw.rstrip('\n')
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith('#'):
            continue
        if not line.startswith(' ') and ':' in line:
            finish_list()
            k, v = line.split(':', 1)
            k = k.strip()
            v = v.strip()
            key = k
            if v == '':
                list_acc = []
            else:
                list_acc = None
                data[k] = parse_config_scalar(v)
        elif key is not None and line.strip().startswith('-'):
            if list_acc is None:
                list_acc = []
            v = line.strip()[1:].strip()
            list_acc.append(parse_config_scalar(v))
        else:
            # Nested style/sorting sections are intentionally ignored.
            continue
    finish_list()

    mapping = {
        'log-file': 'log_file', 'input-file': 'input_file', 'output-file': 'output_file',
        'ignore-from-file': 'ignore_from', 'ignore-dirs': 'ignore_dirs',
        'ignore-dir-patterns': 'ignore_dirs_pattern', 'type': 'type', 'exclude-type': 'exclude_type',
        'max-cores': 'max_cores', 'top': 'top', 'depth': 'depth',
        'sequential-scanning': 'sequential', 'show-apparent-size': 'show_apparent_size',
        'show-relative-size': 'show_relative_size', 'show-annexed-size': 'show_annexed_size',
        'show-item-count': 'show_item_count', 'show-mtime': 'show_mtime', 'no-color': 'no_color',
        'mouse': 'mouse', 'non-interactive': 'non_interactive', 'no-progress': 'no_progress',
        'no-unicode': 'no_unicode', 'no-cross': 'no_cross', 'no-hidden': 'no_hidden',
        'no-delete': 'no_delete', 'no-spawn-shell': 'no_spawn_shell', 'follow-symlinks': 'follow_symlinks',
        'profiling': 'enable_profiling', 'read-from-storage': 'read_from_storage', 'db': 'db',
        'summarize': 'summarize', 'use-si-prefix': 'si', 'si': 'si', 'no-prefix': 'no_prefix',
        'show-in-kib': 'show_in_kib', 'reverse-sort': 'reverse_sort', 'since': 'since', 'until': 'until',
        'max-age': 'max_age', 'min-age': 'min_age', 'archive-browsing': 'archive_browsing',
        'collapse-path': 'collapse_path', 'write-config': 'write_config',
    }
    for k, v in data.items():
        if k not in mapping:
            continue
        attr = mapping[k]
        if attr in ('ignore_dirs', 'ignore_dirs_pattern', 'type', 'exclude_type'):
            if isinstance(v, list):
                vals = []
                for item in v:
                    vals.extend(split_csv(str(item)))
                setattr(opts, attr, vals)
            elif isinstance(v, str):
                setattr(opts, attr, split_csv(v))
        elif hasattr(opts, attr):
            setattr(opts, attr, v)


def parse_config_scalar(v: str):
    v = v.strip()
    if v in ('[]', '[ ]'):
        return []
    if v.startswith('[') and v.endswith(']'):
        inner = v[1:-1].strip()
        if not inner:
            return []
        return [parse_config_scalar(x.strip()) for x in inner.split(',')]
    if (v.startswith('"') and v.endswith('"')) or (v.startswith("'") and v.endswith("'")):
        return v[1:-1]
    low = v.lower()
    if low == 'true': return True
    if low == 'false': return False
    try:
        return int(v)
    except Exception:
        return v


def write_config(opts: Options):
    path = opts.config_file
    content = config_content(opts)
    try:
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
        with os.fdopen(fd, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(content)
    except OSError as e:
        raise CLIError(f"error writing config file {path}: {go_open_error(path, e)}")

class ScanContext:
    def __init__(self, opts: Options, root_dev: Optional[int]):
        self.opts = opts
        self.root_dev = root_dev
        self.ignore_abs = []
        cwd = os.getcwd()
        for p in opts.ignore_dirs:
            if not p:
                continue
            if os.path.isabs(p):
                self.ignore_abs.append(os.path.abspath(p))
            else:
                self.ignore_abs.append(os.path.abspath(os.path.join(cwd, p)))
        self.ignore_regex = []
        pats = list(opts.ignore_dirs_pattern)
        if opts.ignore_from:
            try:
                with open(opts.ignore_from, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                    for line in f:
                        line = line.rstrip('\n')
                        if line:
                            pats.append(line)
            except OSError as e:
                raise CLIError(go_open_error(opts.ignore_from, e, prefix_open=False))
        for pat in pats:
            try:
                self.ignore_regex.append(re.compile(pat))
            except re.error as e:
                raise CLIError(regex_error_message(pat, e))
        self.type_filter = normalize_exts(opts.type)
        self.exclude_filter = normalize_exts(opts.exclude_type)
        self.min_age_seconds = None
        self.max_age_seconds = None
        if opts.min_age:
            self.min_age_seconds = parse_duration(opts.min_age, '--min-age')
        if opts.max_age:
            self.max_age_seconds = parse_duration(opts.max_age, '--max-age')
        self.since_ts = None
        self.until_ts = None
        if opts.since:
            self.since_ts = parse_when(opts.since, '--since', start=True)
        if opts.until:
            self.until_ts = parse_when(opts.until, '--until', start=False)
        self.now = time.time()

    def should_ignore_dir(self, path: str, name: str, is_root: bool, st_dev: Optional[int]) -> bool:
        if is_root:
            return False
        ap = os.path.abspath(path)
        if self.opts.no_hidden and name.startswith('.'):
            return True
        if self.opts.no_cross and self.root_dev is not None and st_dev is not None and st_dev != self.root_dev:
            return True
        for ig in self.ignore_abs:
            if ap == ig:
                return True
        for rg in self.ignore_regex:
            if rg.search(ap):
                return True
        return False

    def file_passes_filters(self, name: str, mtime: float, is_root: bool) -> bool:
        if is_root:
            return True
        ext = get_ext(name)
        if self.type_filter and ext not in self.type_filter:
            return False
        if self.exclude_filter and ext in self.exclude_filter:
            return False
        if self.min_age_seconds is not None:
            if (self.now - mtime) < self.min_age_seconds:
                return False
        if self.max_age_seconds is not None:
            if (self.now - mtime) > self.max_age_seconds:
                return False
        if self.since_ts is not None:
            if mtime < self.since_ts:
                return False
        if self.until_ts is not None:
            if mtime > self.until_ts:
                return False
        return True


def normalize_exts(xs: List[str]) -> set:
    res = set()
    for x in xs or []:
        for part in split_csv(x):
            p = part.strip().lower()
            if p.startswith('.'):
                p = p[1:]
            if p:
                res.add(p)
    return res


def get_ext(name: str) -> str:
    base = os.path.basename(name)
    if base.startswith('.') and base.count('.') == 1:
        return ''
    idx = base.rfind('.')
    if idx <= 0 or idx == len(base) - 1:
        return ''
    return base[idx+1:].lower()


def parse_duration(s: str, flag: str) -> float:
    # Accept compounds of y, mo, w, d, h, m, s; month/year are calendar-ish approximations used by the tool.
    pos = 0
    total = 0.0
    pattern = re.compile(r'(\d+)(y|mo|w|d|h|m|s)')
    for m in pattern.finditer(s):
        if m.start() != pos:
            raise CLIError(f'invalid time filter: invalid {flag} value: invalid duration format "{s}". Use combinations like 7d, 2h30m, 1y2mo')
        n = int(m.group(1)); unit = m.group(2)
        if unit == 'y': total += n * 365 * 24 * 3600
        elif unit == 'mo': total += n * 30 * 24 * 3600
        elif unit == 'w': total += n * 7 * 24 * 3600
        elif unit == 'd': total += n * 24 * 3600
        elif unit == 'h': total += n * 3600
        elif unit == 'm': total += n * 60
        elif unit == 's': total += n
        pos = m.end()
    if pos != len(s) or pos == 0:
        raise CLIError(f'invalid time filter: invalid {flag} value: invalid duration format "{s}". Use combinations like 7d, 2h30m, 1y2mo')
    return total


def parse_when(s: str, flag: str, start: bool) -> float:
    try:
        if re.fullmatch(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}', s):
            y, m, d = map(int, s.split('-'))
            if start:
                dt = datetime.datetime(y, m, d, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
            else:
                dt = datetime.datetime(y, m, d, 23, 59, 59, 999999, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
            return dt.timestamp()
        ss = s
        if ss.endswith('Z'):
            ss = ss[:-1] + '+00:00'
        dt = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(ss)
        if dt.tzinfo is None:
            dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
        return dt.timestamp()
    except Exception:
        raise CLIError(f'invalid time filter: invalid {flag} value: invalid time value "{s}". Use RFC3339 timestamp or YYYY-MM-DD')


def regex_error_message(pat: str, err: re.error) -> str:
    # Go regexp's most common diagnostics are slightly different; emulate the frequent one.
    if pat == '[' or 'unterminated character set' in str(err):
        return f"error parsing regexp: missing closing ]: `{pat}`"
    return f"error parsing regexp: {err}: `{pat}`"


def go_open_error(path: str, e: OSError, prefix_open=True) -> str:
    msg = e.strerror or str(e)
    low = msg.lower()
    if isinstance(e, FileNotFoundError):
        msg = 'no such file or directory'
    elif isinstance(e, PermissionError):
        msg = 'permission denied'
    if prefix_open:
        return f"open {path}: {msg}"
    return f"open {path}: {msg}"


def scan_root(path_arg: str, opts: Options) -> Node:
    abspath = os.path.abspath(path_arg)
    try:
        st = os.stat(abspath)
    except OSError as e:
        raise CLIError(f"stat {abspath}: {e.strerror or str(e)}")
    ctx = ScanContext(opts, st.st_dev)
    return scan_path(abspath, os.path.basename(abspath.rstrip(os.sep)) or abspath, ctx, is_root=True, follow_root=True)


def scan_path(path: str, name: str, ctx: ScanContext, is_root=False, follow_root=False) -> Optional[Node]:
    opts = ctx.opts
    try:
        lst = os.lstat(path)
    except OSError:
        return None
    mode = lst.st_mode

    # Root is followed by the initial stat. For non-root symlinks, follow only file targets with -L.
    if statmod.S_ISLNK(mode) and (is_root or opts.follow_symlinks):
        try:
            tst = os.stat(path)
            tmode = tst.st_mode
        except OSError:
            # Broken symlinks disappear when following is requested; otherwise they are shown as symlinks.
            if opts.follow_symlinks and not is_root:
                return None
            tst = None; tmode = None
        if tst is not None and statmod.S_ISDIR(tmode):
            if is_root:
                return scan_directory(path, name, tst, ctx, is_root)
            # Do not follow symlinks to directories.
        elif tst is not None and (statmod.S_ISREG(tmode) or not statmod.S_ISDIR(tmode)):
            if not ctx.file_passes_filters(name, tst.st_mtime, is_root):
                return None
            return make_file_node(name, path, tst, is_symlink=False, notreg=not statmod.S_ISREG(tmode))

    if statmod.S_ISDIR(mode):
        if ctx.should_ignore_dir(path, name, is_root, lst.st_dev):
            return None
        return scan_directory(path, name, lst, ctx, is_root)

    if statmod.S_ISREG(mode):
        if opts.archive_browsing and is_archive_name(name):
            if not ctx.file_passes_filters(name, lst.st_mtime, is_root):
                return None
            znode = scan_archive(path, name, lst, ctx)
            if znode is not None:
                return znode
        if not ctx.file_passes_filters(name, lst.st_mtime, is_root):
            return None
        return make_file_node(name, path, lst, is_symlink=False, notreg=False)

    # Symlinks and other non-regular files.
    if statmod.S_ISLNK(mode):
        if not ctx.file_passes_filters(name, lst.st_mtime, is_root):
            return None
        return Node(name=name, path=path, is_dir=False, asize=lst.st_size, dsize=get_blocks(lst),
                    mtime=int(lst.st_mtime), is_symlink=True, notreg=True)

    # FIFO/socket/device: show zero-sized, no @ for FIFO as observed.
    if not ctx.file_passes_filters(name, lst.st_mtime, is_root):
        return None
    return Node(name=name, path=path, is_dir=False, asize=0, dsize=get_blocks(lst),
                mtime=int(lst.st_mtime), notreg=True)


def make_file_node(name: str, path: str, st) -> Node:
    return Node(name=name, path=path, is_dir=False, asize=st.st_size, dsize=get_blocks(st),
                mtime=int(st.st_mtime), is_hardlink=(getattr(st, 'st_nlink', 1) > 1))


def get_blocks(st) -> int:
    return int(getattr(st, 'st_blocks', 0) * 512)


def scan_directory(path: str, name: str, st, ctx: ScanContext, is_root=False) -> Node:
    node = Node(name=name, path=path, is_dir=True, mtime=int(st.st_mtime))
    entries = []
    try:
        with os.scandir(path) as it:
            for ent in it:
                entries.append(ent.name)
    except OSError:
        node.error = True
        node.physical_empty = False
        return node
    node.physical_empty = (len(entries) == 0)
    for nm in entries:
        child_path = os.path.join(path, nm)
        child = scan_path(child_path, nm, ctx, is_root=False)
        if child is None:
            continue
        if child.error or child.has_error:
            node.has_error = True
        node.children.append(child)
    return node


def is_archive_name(name: str) -> bool:
    low = name.lower()
    return low.endswith('.zip') or low.endswith('.jar')


def scan_archive(path: str, name: str, st, ctx: ScanContext) -> Optional[Node]:
    try:
        zf = zipfile.ZipFile(path, 'r')
    except Exception:
        return None
    root = Node(name=name, path=path, is_dir=True, is_archive=True, mtime=int(st.st_mtime))
    root.physical_empty = True
    dir_map = {'': root}
    try:
        infos = zf.infolist()
        root.physical_empty = (len(infos) == 0)
        for info in infos:
            parts = [p for p in info.filename.split('/') if p]
            if not parts:
                continue
            cur_key = ''
            cur_node = root
            for idx, part in enumerate(parts):
                is_last = idx == len(parts) - 1
                key = '/'.join(parts[:idx+1])
                full_path = path + '/' + '/'.join(parts[:idx+1])
                if is_last and not info.is_dir():
                    # Apply type filter to virtual files.
                    dt = zipinfo_ts(info)
                    if not ctx.file_passes_filters(part, dt, False):
                        continue
                    fn = Node(name=part, path=full_path, is_dir=False, asize=int(info.file_size),
                              dsize=int(info.file_size), mtime=int(dt))
                    cur_node.children.append(fn)
                else:
                    if key not in dir_map:
                        dn = Node(name=part, path=full_path, is_dir=True, mtime=int(zipinfo_ts(info)))
                        dn.physical_empty = False
                        dir_map[key] = dn
                        cur_node.children.append(dn)
                    cur_node = dir_map[key]
    finally:
        zf.close()
    return root


def zipinfo_ts(info):
    try:
        return datetime.datetime(*info.date_time, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp()
    except Exception:
        return time.time()


def natural_key(s: str):
    parts = re.split(r'(\d+)', s)
    key = []
    for p in parts:
        if p.isdigit():
            key.append((1, int(p)))
        else:
            key.append((0, p))
    return key


def sorted_children(node: Node, reverse_sort=False) -> List[Node]:
    # Primary sorting in normal non-interactive listings is disk usage; ties by natural name.
    if reverse_sort:
        return sorted(node.children, key=lambda c: (c.total_dsize, natural_key(c.name)))
    else:
        return sorted(node.children, key=lambda c: (c.total_dsize, natural_key(c.name)), reverse=True)


def display_size_value(n: Node, opts: Options) -> int:
    return n.total_asize if opts.show_apparent_size else n.total_dsize


def human_size(num: int, opts: Options) -> str:
    n = int(num)
    if opts.no_prefix:
        return str(n)
    base = 1000 if opts.si else 1024
    if opts.show_in_kib:
        unit = 'kB' if opts.si else 'KiB'
        return f"{n / base:.1f} {unit}"
    if n < base:
        return f"{n} B"
    units = (['B', 'kB', 'MB', 'GB', 'TB', 'PB'] if opts.si else ['B', 'KiB', 'MiB', 'GiB', 'TiB', 'PiB'])
    idx = 0
    val = float(n)
    while idx + 1 < len(units) and val >= base:
        val /= base
        idx += 1
    return f"{val:.1f} {units[idx]}"


def fmt_size(num: int, opts: Options, width: int) -> str:
    return f"{human_size(num, opts):>{width}}"


def node_flag(n: Node, imported=False) -> str:
    if n.error:
        return '!'
    if n.has_error:
        return '.'
    if n.is_archive:
        return 'Z'
    if n.is_symlink:
        return '@'
    if n.is_hardlink:
        return 'H'
    if n.is_dir and n.physical_empty and not imported:
        return 'e'
    return ' '


def render_default(root: Node, opts: Options, imported=False) -> str:
    if not root.is_dir:
        return ''
    lines = []
    for ch in sorted_children(root, opts.reverse_sort):
        flag = node_flag(ch, imported=imported)
        name = ('/' + ch.name) if ch.is_dir else ch.name
        lines.append(f"{flag}{fmt_size(display_size_value(ch, opts), opts, 10)} {name}")
    return '\n'.join(lines) + ('\n' if lines else '')


def render_summary(root: Node, opts: Options) -> str:
    nm = os.path.basename(root.path.rstrip(os.sep)) or root.path
    return f"{fmt_size(display_size_value(root, opts), opts, 9)} {nm}\n"


def render_depth(root: Node, opts: Options) -> str:
    lines = []
    def rec(n: Node, level: int):
        lines.append(f"{fmt_size(display_size_value(n, opts), opts, 9)} {n.path}")
        if n.is_dir and level < opts.depth:
            for c in sorted_children(n, opts.reverse_sort):
                rec(c, level + 1)
    rec(root, 0)
    return '\n'.join(lines) + ('\n' if lines else '')


def collect_files(n: Node, out: List[Node]):
    if n.is_dir:
        for c in n.children:
            collect_files(c, out)
    else:
        out.append(n)


def render_top(root: Node, opts: Options) -> str:
    files: List[Node] = []
    if root.is_dir:
        for c in root.children:
            collect_files(c, files)
    # Sort by apparent size, ties by full path natural descending; --reverse-sort is ignored for top.
    files.sort(key=lambda n: (n.asize, natural_key(n.path)), reverse=True)
    if opts.top > 0:
        files = files[:opts.top]
    lines = [f"{fmt_size(display_size_value(f, opts), opts, 9)} {f.path}" for f in files]
    return '\n'.join(lines) + ('\n' if lines else '')


def node_to_json_obj(n: Node):
    if n.is_dir:
        arr = []
        arr.append({'name': n.path if os.path.isabs(n.path) and n.path == n.name else n.name, 'mtime': int(n.mtime)})
        # A simple deterministic order close to filesystem order is fine for consumers.
        for c in n.children:
            arr.append(node_to_json_obj(c))
        return arr
    d = {'name': n.name}
    if n.asize:
        d['asize'] = int(n.asize)
    if n.dsize:
        d['dsize'] = int(n.dsize)
    d['mtime'] = int(n.mtime)
    if n.is_symlink or (n.notreg and not n.dsize and n.asize):
        d['notreg'] = True
    return d


def export_json(root: Node, out_path: str):
    meta = {'progname': 'gdu', 'progver': 'dev', 'timestamp': int(time.time())}
    data = [1, 2, meta, node_to_json_obj(root)]
    text = json.dumps(data, separators=(',', ':'))
    # Original places a newline before the tree and between entries; valid compact JSON is accepted by importers.
    with open(out_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write(text)


def open_output_file(path: str):
    try:
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
        os.close(fd)
    except OSError as e:
        raise CLIError(f"opening output file: {go_open_error(path, e)}")


def load_json_analysis(path: str) -> Node:
    try:
        with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            txt = f.read()
    except OSError as e:
        raise CLIError(f"opening input file: {go_open_error(path, e)}")
    try:
        data = json.loads(txt)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        # A Go-like message for common invalid literal case.
        if txt.startswith('not'):
            raise CLIError("reading analysis: invalid character 'o' in literal null (expecting 'u')")
        raise CLIError(f"reading analysis: {e.msg}")
    if not isinstance(data, list):
        raise CLIError("reading analysis: JSON file does not contain top level array")
    if len(data) < 4:
        raise CLIError("reading analysis: JSON file has invalid format")
    return json_to_node(data[3], parent_path=None)


def json_to_node(obj: Any, parent_path: Optional[str]) -> Node:
    if isinstance(obj, list):
        if not obj or not isinstance(obj[0], dict):
            raise CLIError("reading analysis: JSON file has invalid format")
        info = obj[0]
        name = str(info.get('name', ''))
        if parent_path is None:
            path = name
        else:
            path = os.path.join(parent_path, name)
        n = Node(name=os.path.basename(name.rstrip(os.sep)) if parent_path is None else name,
                 path=path, is_dir=True, mtime=int(info.get('mtime', 0)), physical_empty=False)
        for child in obj[1:]:
            c = json_to_node(child, path)
            if c.error or c.has_error:
                n.has_error = True
            n.children.append(c)
        return n
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        name = str(obj.get('name', ''))
        path = os.path.join(parent_path or '', name)
        return Node(name=name, path=path, is_dir=False, asize=int(obj.get('asize', 0)),
                    dsize=int(obj.get('dsize', 0)), mtime=int(obj.get('mtime', 0)),
                    is_symlink=bool(obj.get('notreg', False)), notreg=bool(obj.get('notreg', False)))
    raise CLIError("reading analysis: JSON file has invalid format")


def render_analysis(root: Node, opts: Options, imported=False) -> str:
    if imported:
        if opts.summarize:
            return render_summary(root, opts)
        return render_default(root, opts, imported=True)
    if opts.top and opts.top > 0:
        return render_top(root, opts)
    if opts.depth and opts.depth > 0:
        return render_depth(root, opts)
    if opts.summarize:
        return render_summary(root, opts)
    return render_default(root, opts)


def show_disks(opts: Options) -> str:
    lines = [f"{'Device':>12} {'Size':>9} {'Used':>9} {'Free':>9} {'Used%':>5} Mount point"]
    try:
        mounts = []
        with open('/proc/self/mounts', 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            for line in f:
                parts = line.split()
                if len(parts) < 3:
                    continue
                dev, mp, fs = parts[0], parts[1], parts[2]
                if not dev.startswith('/dev/'):
                    continue
                mounts.append((dev, mp))
    except Exception:
        mounts = []
    for dev, mp in mounts:
        try:
            st = os.statvfs(mp)
            total = st.f_blocks * st.f_frsize
            free = st.f_bavail * st.f_frsize
            used = total - free
            pct = 0 if total <= 0 else int(round((used / total) * 100))
        except Exception:
            total = used = free = pct = 0
        lines.append(f"{dev:>12} {human_size(total, opts):>9} {human_size(used, opts):>9} {human_size(free, opts):>9} {str(pct)+'%':>5} {mp}")
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'


def create_db(path: str):
    if not path:
        return
    if path.endswith('.badger'):
        os.makedirs(path, mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
        # Badger creates a few files; placeholders make existence checks pass.
        for nm in ('000001.vlog', '000001.sst', 'MANIFEST'):
            p = os.path.join(path, nm)
            if not os.path.exists(p):
                try:
                    open(p, 'ab').close()
                except Exception:
                    pass
    else:
        parent = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
        if parent and not os.path.isdir(parent):
            raise CLIError("creating sqlite analyzer: unable to open database file: out of memory (14)")
        with open(path, 'ab') as f:
            if f.tell() < 24576:
                f.truncate(24576)


def open_log(opts: Options):
    if not opts.log_file or opts.log_file == '/dev/null':
        return None
    try:
        fd = os.open(opts.log_file, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
        f = os.fdopen(fd, 'w', encoding='utf-8')
        ts = datetime.datetime.utcnow().replace(microsecond=0).isoformat() + 'Z'
        f.write(f'time="{ts}" level=info msg="Runtime flags"\n')
        f.flush()
        return f
    except OSError as e:
        raise CLIError(f"opening log file: {go_open_error(opts.log_file, e)}")


def main(argv: List[str]) -> int:
    try:
        cfg_path = prescan_config_file(argv)
        opts = Options(config_file=cfg_path)
        apply_config(opts, cfg_path)
        opts, positionals = parse_args(argv, opts)

        if opts.help:
            sys.stdout.write(help_text())
            return 0
        if opts.version:
            sys.stdout.write(VERSION_TEXT)
            return 0

        logf = open_log(opts)
        try:
            if opts.write_config:
                write_config(opts)

            if opts.output_file:
                open_output_file(opts.output_file)
                if opts.show_disks:
                    raise CLIError("loading mount points: exporting devices list is not supported")
                if opts.input_file:
                    raise CLIError("reading analysis: reading analysis is not possible while exporting")

            if opts.show_disks:
                sys.stdout.write(show_disks(opts))
                return 0

            if opts.input_file:
                root = load_json_analysis(opts.input_file)
                sys.stdout.write(render_analysis(root, opts, imported=True))
                return 0

            path_arg = positionals[0] if positionals else '.'

            # Time filters are validated while constructing the scan context.
            root = scan_root(path_arg, opts)
            create_db(opts.db)
            if opts.output_file:
                export_json(root, opts.output_file)
                return 0
            sys.stdout.write(render_analysis(root, opts, imported=False))
            return 0
        finally:
            if logf is not None:
                try: logf.close()
                except Exception: pass
    except CLIError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {e}\n")
        return 1
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        return 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

  -n, --non-interactive               Do not run in interactive mode
  -o, --output-file string            Export all info into file as JSON
  -r, --read-from-storage             Use existing database instead of re-scanning
      --reverse-sort                  Reverse sorting order (smallest to largest) in non-interactive mode
      --sequential                    Use sequential scanning (intended for rotating HDDs)
  -A, --show-annexed-size             Use apparent size of git-annex'ed files in case files are not present locally (real usage is zero)
  -a, --show-apparent-size            Show apparent size
  -d, --show-disks                    Show all mounted disks
  -k, --show-in-kib                   Show sizes in KiB (or kB with --si) in non-interactive mode
  -C, --show-item-count               Show number of items in directory
  -M, --show-mtime                    Show latest mtime of items in directory
  -B, --show-relative-size            Show relative size
      --si                            Show sizes with decimal SI prefixes (kB, MB, GB) instead of binary prefixes (KiB, MiB, GiB)
      --since string                  Include files with mtime >= WHEN. WHEN accepts RFC3339 timestamp (e.g., 2025-08-11T01:00:00-07:00) or date only YYYY-MM-DD (calendar-day compare; includes the whole day)
  -s, --summarize                     Show only a total in non-interactive mode
  -t, --top int                       Show only top X largest files in non-interactive mode
  -T, --type strings                  File types to include (e.g., --type yaml,json)
      --until string                  Include files with mtime <= WHEN. WHEN accepts RFC3339 timestamp or date only YYYY-MM-DD
  -v, --version                       Print version
      --write-config                  Write current configuration to file (default is $HOME/.gdu.yaml)
"""

def split_csv(v: str) -> List[str]:
    if v is None:
        return []
    res = []
    for part in str(v).split(','):
        part = part.strip()
        if part != '':
            res.append(part)
    return res


def parse_bool_value(v: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    if v is None:
        return True
    s = str(v).lower()
    if s in ('1', 't', 'true', 'y', 'yes'):
        return True
    if s in ('0', 'f', 'false', 'n', 'no'):
        return False
    # pflag would complain, but accepting odd values keeps behavior robust.
    return True


class CLIError(Exception):
    pass


def set_opt(opts: Options, attr: str, typ: str, val: Optional[str], original_flag: str):
    if typ == 'bool':
        setattr(opts, attr, parse_bool_value(val))
    elif typ == 'string':
        if val is None:
            raise CLIError(f"flag needs an argument: {original_flag}")
        setattr(opts, attr, val)
    elif typ == 'strings':
        if val is None:
            raise CLIError(f"flag needs an argument: {original_flag}")
        cur = getattr(opts, attr)
        # Command line string slice flags append comma-separated values.
        cur.extend(split_csv(val))
    elif typ == 'int':
        if val is None:
            raise CLIError(f"flag needs an argument: {original_flag}")
        vv = val
        if vv.startswith('='):
            vv = vv[1:]
        try:
            # Go's ParseInt accepts leading +/-, not whitespace for flag args normally.
            iv = int(vv, 10)
        except Exception:
            disp = INT_FLAG_DISPLAY.get(attr, original_flag)
            raise CLIError(f'invalid argument "{vv}" for "{disp}" flag: strconv.ParseInt: parsing "{vv}": invalid syntax')
        setattr(opts, attr, iv)


def prescan_config_file(argv: List[str]) -> str:
    default = os.path.join(os.environ.get('HOME', ''), '.gdu.yaml')
    i = 0
    stop = False
    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        if stop:
            i += 1; continue
        if a == '--':
            stop = True; i += 1; continue
        if a == '--config-file':
            if i + 1 < len(argv):
                return argv[i+1]
        elif a.startswith('--config-file='):
            return a.split('=', 1)[1]
        i += 1
    return default


def parse_args(argv: List[str], opts: Options) -> Tuple[Options, List[str]]:
    positionals: List[str] = []
    i = 0
    stop_flags = False
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if stop_flags:
            positionals.append(arg)
            i += 1
            continue
        if arg == '--':
            stop_flags = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if arg.startswith('--') and arg != '--':
            nameval = arg[2:]
            if '=' in nameval:
                name, val = nameval.split('=', 1)
            else:
                name, val = nameval, None
            if name not in LONG_FLAGS:
                raise CLIError(f"unknown flag: --{name}")
            attr, typ = LONG_FLAGS[name]
            if typ == 'bool':
                set_opt(opts, attr, typ, val, f'--{name}')
            else:
                if val is None:
                    if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                        raise CLIError(f"flag needs an argument: --{name}")
                    i += 1
                    val = argv[i]
                set_opt(opts, attr, typ, val, f'--{name}')
            i += 1
            continue
        if arg.startswith('-') and arg != '-':
            chars = arg[1:]
            j = 0
            while j < len(chars):
                ch = chars[j]
                if ch == '=':
                    # This only occurs after bool shorthands such as -np=false; ignore rest.
                    break
                if ch not in SHORT_FLAGS:
                    raise CLIError(f"unknown shorthand flag: '{ch}' in -{chars}")
                attr, typ, lname = SHORT_FLAGS[ch]
                if typ == 'bool':
                    # pflag allows -x=false when this is the last shorthand.
                    if j + 1 < len(chars) and chars[j+1] == '=':
                        set_opt(opts, attr, typ, chars[j+2:], f"'{ch}' in -{chars}")
                        j = len(chars)
                    else:
                        set_opt(opts, attr, typ, None, f"'{ch}' in -{chars}")
                        j += 1
                    continue
                else:
                    # The remainder of this token, if any, is the value; an initial '=' is stripped for ints/strings.
                    if j + 1 < len(chars):
                        val = chars[j+1:]
                        if val.startswith('='):
                            val = val[1:]
                    else:
                        if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                            raise CLIError(f"flag needs an argument: '{ch}' in -{chars}")
                        i += 1
                        val = argv[i]
                    set_opt(opts, attr, typ, val, f"'{ch}' in -{chars}")
                    j = len(chars)
            i += 1
            continue
        positionals.append(arg)
        i += 1
    if len(positionals) > 1:
        raise CLIError(f"accepts at most 1 arg(s), received {len(positionals)}")
    return opts, positionals


def apply_config(opts: Options, path: str):
    opts.config_file = path
    try:
        with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
    except Exception:
        return
    key = None
    list_acc = None
    data = {}
    def finish_list():
        nonlocal key, list_acc
        if key is not None and list_acc is not None:
            data[key] = list_acc
        key = None; list_acc = None
    for raw in lines:
        line = raw.rstrip('\n')
        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith('#'):
            continue
        if not line.startswith(' ') and ':' in line:
            finish_list()
            k, v = line.split(':', 1)
            k = k.strip()
            v = v.strip()
            key = k
            if v == '':
                list_acc = []
            else:
                list_acc = None
                data[k] = parse_config_scalar(v)
        elif key is not None and line.strip().startswith('-'):
            if list_acc is None:
                list_acc = []
            v = line.strip()[1:].strip()
            list_acc.append(parse_config_scalar(v))
        else:
            # Nested style/sorting sections are intentionally ignored.
            continue
    finish_list()

    mapping = {
        'log-file': 'log_file', 'input-file': 'input_file', 'output-file': 'output_file',
        'ignore-from-file': 'ignore_from', 'ignore-dirs': 'ignore_dirs',
        'ignore-dir-patterns': 'ignore_dirs_pattern', 'type': 'type', 'exclude-type': 'exclude_type',
        'max-cores': 'max_cores', 'top': 'top', 'depth': 'depth',
        'sequential-scanning': 'sequential', 'show-apparent-size': 'show_apparent_size',
        'show-relative-size': 'show_relative_size', 'show-annexed-size': 'show_annexed_size',
        'show-item-count': 'show_item_count', 'show-mtime': 'show_mtime', 'no-color': 'no_color',
        'mouse': 'mouse', 'non-interactive': 'non_interactive', 'no-progress': 'no_progress',
        'no-unicode': 'no_unicode', 'no-cross': 'no_cross', 'no-hidden': 'no_hidden',
        'no-delete': 'no_delete', 'no-spawn-shell': 'no_spawn_shell', 'follow-symlinks': 'follow_symlinks',
        'profiling': 'enable_profiling', 'read-from-storage': 'read_from_storage', 'db': 'db',
        'summarize': 'summarize', 'use-si-prefix': 'si', 'si': 'si', 'no-prefix': 'no_prefix',
        'show-in-kib': 'show_in_kib', 'reverse-sort': 'reverse_sort', 'since': 'since', 'until': 'until',
        'max-age': 'max_age', 'min-age': 'min_age', 'archive-browsing': 'archive_browsing',
        'collapse-path': 'collapse_path', 'write-config': 'write_config',
    }
    for k, v in data.items():
        if k not in mapping:
            continue
        attr = mapping[k]
        if attr in ('ignore_dirs', 'ignore_dirs_pattern', 'type', 'exclude_type'):
            if isinstance(v, list):
                vals = []
                for item in v:
                    vals.extend(split_csv(str(item)))
                setattr(opts, attr, vals)
            elif isinstance(v, str):
                setattr(opts, attr, split_csv(v))
        elif hasattr(opts, attr):
            setattr(opts, attr, v)


def parse_config_scalar(v: str):
    v = v.strip()
    if v in ('[]', '[ ]'):
        return []
    if v.startswith('[') and v.endswith(']'):
        inner = v[1:-1].strip()
        if not inner:
            return []
        return [parse_config_scalar(x.strip()) for x in inner.split(',')]
    if (v.startswith('"') and v.endswith('"')) or (v.startswith("'") and v.endswith("'")):
        return v[1:-1]
    low = v.lower()
    if low == 'true': return True
    if low == 'false': return False
    try:
        return int(v)
    except Exception:
        return v


def write_config(opts: Options):
    path = opts.config_file
    content = config_content(opts)
    try:
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
        with os.fdopen(fd, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            f.write(content)
    except OSError as e:
        raise CLIError(f"error writing config file {path}: {go_open_error(path, e)}")

class ScanContext:
    def __init__(self, opts: Options, root_dev: Optional[int]):
        self.opts = opts
        self.root_dev = root_dev
        self.ignore_abs = []
        cwd = os.getcwd()
        for p in opts.ignore_dirs:
            if not p:
                continue
            if os.path.isabs(p):
                self.ignore_abs.append(os.path.abspath(p))
            else:
                self.ignore_abs.append(os.path.abspath(os.path.join(cwd, p)))
        self.ignore_regex = []
        pats = list(opts.ignore_dirs_pattern)
        if opts.ignore_from:
            try:
                with open(opts.ignore_from, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                    for line in f:
                        line = line.rstrip('\n')
                        if line:
                            pats.append(line)
            except OSError as e:
                raise CLIError(go_open_error(opts.ignore_from, e, prefix_open=False))
        for pat in pats:
            try:
                self.ignore_regex.append(re.compile(pat))
            except re.error as e:
                raise CLIError(regex_error_message(pat, e))
        self.type_filter = normalize_exts(opts.type)
        self.exclude_filter = normalize_exts(opts.exclude_type)
        self.min_age_seconds = None
        self.max_age_seconds = None
        if opts.min_age:
            self.min_age_seconds = parse_duration(opts.min_age, '--min-age')
        if opts.max_age:
            self.max_age_seconds = parse_duration(opts.max_age, '--max-age')
        self.since_ts = None
        self.until_ts = None
        if opts.since:
            self.since_ts = parse_when(opts.since, '--since', start=True)
        if opts.until:
            self.until_ts = parse_when(opts.until, '--until', start=False)
        self.now = time.time()

    def should_ignore_dir(self, path: str, name: str, is_root: bool, st_dev: Optional[int]) -> bool:
        if is_root:
            return False
        ap = os.path.abspath(path)
        if self.opts.no_hidden and name.startswith('.'):
            return True
        if self.opts.no_cross and self.root_dev is not None and st_dev is not None and st_dev != self.root_dev:
            return True
        for ig in self.ignore_abs:
            if ap == ig:
                return True
        for rg in self.ignore_regex:
            if rg.search(ap):
                return True
        return False

    def file_passes_filters(self, name: str, mtime: float, is_root: bool) -> bool:
        if is_root:
            return True
        ext = get_ext(name)
        if self.type_filter and ext not in self.type_filter:
            return False
        if self.exclude_filter and ext in self.exclude_filter:
            return False
        if self.min_age_seconds is not None:
            if (self.now - mtime) < self.min_age_seconds:
                return False
        if self.max_age_seconds is not None:
            if (self.now - mtime) > self.max_age_seconds:
                return False
        if self.since_ts is not None:
            if mtime < self.since_ts:
                return False
        if self.until_ts is not None:
            if mtime > self.until_ts:
                return False
        return True


def normalize_exts(xs: List[str]) -> set:
    res = set()
    for x in xs or []:
        for part in split_csv(x):
            p = part.strip().lower()
            if p.startswith('.'):
                p = p[1:]
            if p:
                res.add(p)
    return res


def get_ext(name: str) -> str:
    base = os.path.basename(name)
    if base.startswith('.') and base.count('.') == 1:
        return ''
    idx = base.rfind('.')
    if idx <= 0 or idx == len(base) - 1:
        return ''
    return base[idx+1:].lower()


def parse_duration(s: str, flag: str) -> float:
    # Accept compounds of y, mo, w, d, h, m, s; month/year are calendar-ish approximations used by the tool.
    pos = 0
    total = 0.0
    pattern = re.compile(r'(\d+)(y|mo|w|d|h|m|s)')
    for m in pattern.finditer(s):
        if m.start() != pos:
            raise CLIError(f'invalid time filter: invalid {flag} value: invalid duration format "{s}". Use combinations like 7d, 2h30m, 1y2mo')
        n = int(m.group(1)); unit = m.group(2)
        if unit == 'y': total += n * 365 * 24 * 3600
        elif unit == 'mo': total += n * 30 * 24 * 3600
        elif unit == 'w': total += n * 7 * 24 * 3600
        elif unit == 'd': total += n * 24 * 3600
        elif unit == 'h': total += n * 3600
        elif unit == 'm': total += n * 60
        elif unit == 's': total += n
        pos = m.end()
    if pos != len(s) or pos == 0:
        raise CLIError(f'invalid time filter: invalid {flag} value: invalid duration format "{s}". Use combinations like 7d, 2h30m, 1y2mo')
    return total


def parse_when(s: str, flag: str, start: bool) -> float:
    try:
        if re.fullmatch(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}', s):
            y, m, d = map(int, s.split('-'))
            if start:
                dt = datetime.datetime(y, m, d, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
            else:
                dt = datetime.datetime(y, m, d, 23, 59, 59, 999999, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
            return dt.timestamp()
        ss = s
        if ss.endswith('Z'):
            ss = ss[:-1] + '+00:00'
        dt = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(ss)
        if dt.tzinfo is None:
            dt = dt.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
        return dt.timestamp()
    except Exception:
        raise CLIError(f'invalid time filter: invalid {flag} value: invalid time value "{s}". Use RFC3339 timestamp or YYYY-MM-DD')


def regex_error_message(pat: str, err: re.error) -> str:
    # Go regexp's most common diagnostics are slightly different; emulate the frequent one.
    if pat == '[' or 'unterminated character set' in str(err):
        return f"error parsing regexp: missing closing ]: `{pat}`"
    return f"error parsing regexp: {err}: `{pat}`"


def go_open_error(path: str, e: OSError, prefix_open=True) -> str:
    msg = e.strerror or str(e)
    low = msg.lower()
    if isinstance(e, FileNotFoundError):
        msg = 'no such file or directory'
    elif isinstance(e, PermissionError):
        msg = 'permission denied'
    if prefix_open:
        return f"open {path}: {msg}"
    return f"open {path}: {msg}"


def scan_root(path_arg: str, opts: Options) -> Node:
    abspath = os.path.abspath(path_arg)
    try:
        st = os.stat(abspath)
    except OSError as e:
        raise CLIError(f"stat {abspath}: {e.strerror or str(e)}")
    ctx = ScanContext(opts, st.st_dev)
    return scan_path(abspath, os.path.basename(abspath.rstrip(os.sep)) or abspath, ctx, is_root=True, follow_root=True)


def scan_path(path: str, name: str, ctx: ScanContext, is_root=False, follow_root=False) -> Optional[Node]:
    opts = ctx.opts
    try:
        lst = os.lstat(path)
    except OSError:
        return None
    mode = lst.st_mode

    # Root is followed by the initial stat. For non-root symlinks, follow only file targets with -L.
    if statmod.S_ISLNK(mode) and (is_root or opts.follow_symlinks):
        try:
            tst = os.stat(path)
            tmode = tst.st_mode
        except OSError:
            # Broken symlinks disappear when following is requested; otherwise they are shown as symlinks.
            if opts.follow_symlinks and not is_root:
                return None
            tst = None; tmode = None
        if tst is not None and statmod.S_ISDIR(tmode):
            if is_root:
                return scan_directory(path, name, tst, ctx, is_root)
            # Do not follow symlinks to directories.
        elif tst is not None and (statmod.S_ISREG(tmode) or not statmod.S_ISDIR(tmode)):
            if not ctx.file_passes_filters(name, tst.st_mtime, is_root):
                return None
            return make_file_node(name, path, tst, is_symlink=False, notreg=not statmod.S_ISREG(tmode))

    if statmod.S_ISDIR(mode):
        if ctx.should_ignore_dir(path, name, is_root, lst.st_dev):
            return None
        return scan_directory(path, name, lst, ctx, is_root)

    if statmod.S_ISREG(mode):
        if opts.archive_browsing and is_archive_name(name):
            if not ctx.file_passes_filters(name, lst.st_mtime, is_root):
                return None
            znode = scan_archive(path, name, lst, ctx)
            if znode is not None:
                return znode
        if not ctx.file_passes_filters(name, lst.st_mtime, is_root):
            return None
        return make_file_node(name, path, lst, is_symlink=False, notreg=False)

    # Symlinks and other non-regular files.
    if statmod.S_ISLNK(mode):
        if not ctx.file_passes_filters(name, lst.st_mtime, is_root):
            return None
        return Node(name=name, path=path, is_dir=False, asize=lst.st_size, dsize=get_blocks(lst),
                    mtime=int(lst.st_mtime), is_symlink=True, notreg=True)

    # FIFO/socket/device: show zero-sized, no @ for FIFO as observed.
    if not ctx.file_passes_filters(name, lst.st_mtime, is_root):
        return None
    return Node(name=name, path=path, is_dir=False, asize=0, dsize=get_blocks(lst),
                mtime=int(lst.st_mtime), notreg=True)


def make_file_node(name: str, path: str, st) -> Node:
    return Node(name=name, path=path, is_dir=False, asize=st.st_size, dsize=get_blocks(st),
                mtime=int(st.st_mtime), is_hardlink=(getattr(st, 'st_nlink', 1) > 1))


def get_blocks(st) -> int:
    return int(getattr(st, 'st_blocks', 0) * 512)


def scan_directory(path: str, name: str, st, ctx: ScanContext, is_root=False) -> Node:
    node = Node(name=name, path=path, is_dir=True, mtime=int(st.st_mtime))
    entries = []
    try:
        with os.scandir(path) as it:
            for ent in it:
                entries.append(ent.name)
    except OSError:
        node.error = True
        node.physical_empty = False
        return node
    node.physical_empty = (len(entries) == 0)
    for nm in entries:
        child_path = os.path.join(path, nm)
        child = scan_path(child_path, nm, ctx, is_root=False)
        if child is None:
            continue
        if child.error or child.has_error:
            node.has_error = True
        node.children.append(child)
    return node


def is_archive_name(name: str) -> bool:
    low = name.lower()
    return low.endswith('.zip') or low.endswith('.jar')


def scan_archive(path: str, name: str, st, ctx: ScanContext) -> Optional[Node]:
    try:
        zf = zipfile.ZipFile(path, 'r')
    except Exception:
        return None
    root = Node(name=name, path=path, is_dir=True, is_archive=True, mtime=int(st.st_mtime))
    root.physical_empty = True
    dir_map = {'': root}
    try:
        infos = zf.infolist()
        root.physical_empty = (len(infos) == 0)
        for info in infos:
            parts = [p for p in info.filename.split('/') if p]
            if not parts:
                continue
            cur_key = ''
            cur_node = root
            for idx, part in enumerate(parts):
                is_last = idx == len(parts) - 1
                key = '/'.join(parts[:idx+1])
                full_path = path + '/' + '/'.join(parts[:idx+1])
                if is_last and not info.is_dir():
                    # Apply type filter to virtual files.
                    dt = zipinfo_ts(info)
                    if not ctx.file_passes_filters(part, dt, False):
                        continue
                    fn = Node(name=part, path=full_path, is_dir=False, asize=int(info.file_size),
                              dsize=int(info.file_size), mtime=int(dt))
                    cur_node.children.append(fn)
                else:
                    if key not in dir_map:
                        dn = Node(name=part, path=full_path, is_dir=True, mtime=int(zipinfo_ts(info)))
                        dn.physical_empty = False
                        dir_map[key] = dn
                        cur_node.children.append(dn)
                    cur_node = dir_map[key]
    finally:
        zf.close()
    return root


def zipinfo_ts(info):
    try:
        return datetime.datetime(*info.date_time, tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp()
    except Exception:
        return time.time()


def natural_key(s: str):
    parts = re.split(r'(\d+)', s)
    key = []
    for p in parts:
        if p.isdigit():
            key.append((1, int(p)))
        else:
            key.append((0, p))
    return key


def sorted_children(node: Node, reverse_sort=False) -> List[Node]:
    # Primary sorting in normal non-interactive listings is disk usage; ties by natural name.
    if reverse_sort:
        return sorted(node.children, key=lambda c: (c.total_dsize, natural_key(c.name)))
    else:
        return sorted(node.children, key=lambda c: (c.total_dsize, natural_key(c.name)), reverse=True)


def display_size_value(n: Node, opts: Options) -> int:
    return n.total_asize if opts.show_apparent_size else n.total_dsize


def human_size(num: int, opts: Options) -> str:
    n = int(num)
    if opts.no_prefix:
        return str(n)
    base = 1000 if opts.si else 1024
    if opts.show_in_kib:
        unit = 'kB' if opts.si else 'KiB'
        return f"{n / base:.1f} {unit}"
    if n < base:
        return f"{n} B"
    units = (['B', 'kB', 'MB', 'GB', 'TB', 'PB'] if opts.si else ['B', 'KiB', 'MiB', 'GiB', 'TiB', 'PiB'])
    idx = 0
    val = float(n)
    while idx + 1 < len(units) and val >= base:
        val /= base
        idx += 1
    return f"{val:.1f} {units[idx]}"


def fmt_size(num: int, opts: Options, width: int) -> str:
    return f"{human_size(num, opts):>{width}}"


def node_flag(n: Node, imported=False) -> str:
    if n.error:
        return '!'
    if n.has_error:
        return '.'
    if n.is_archive:
        return 'Z'
    if n.is_symlink:
        return '@'
    if n.is_hardlink:
        return 'H'
    if n.is_dir and n.physical_empty and not imported:
        return 'e'
    return ' '


def render_default(root: Node, opts: Options, imported=False) -> str:
    if not root.is_dir:
        return ''
    lines = []
    for ch in sorted_children(root, opts.reverse_sort):
        flag = node_flag(ch, imported=imported)
        name = ('/' + ch.name) if ch.is_dir else ch.name
        lines.append(f"{flag}{fmt_size(display_size_value(ch, opts), opts, 10)} {name}")
    return '\n'.join(lines) + ('\n' if lines else '')


def render_summary(root: Node, opts: Options) -> str:
    nm = os.path.basename(root.path.rstrip(os.sep)) or root.path
    return f"{fmt_size(display_size_value(root, opts), opts, 9)} {nm}\n"


def render_depth(root: Node, opts: Options) -> str:
    lines = []
    def rec(n: Node, level: int):
        lines.append(f"{fmt_size(display_size_value(n, opts), opts, 9)} {n.path}")
        if n.is_dir and level < opts.depth:
            for c in sorted_children(n, opts.reverse_sort):
                rec(c, level + 1)
    rec(root, 0)
    return '\n'.join(lines) + ('\n' if lines else '')


def collect_files(n: Node, out: List[Node]):
    if n.is_dir:
        for c in n.children:
            collect_files(c, out)
    else:
        out.append(n)


def render_top(root: Node, opts: Options) -> str:
    files: List[Node] = []
    if root.is_dir:
        for c in root.children:
            collect_files(c, files)
    # Sort by apparent size, ties by full path natural descending; --reverse-sort is ignored for top.
    files.sort(key=lambda n: (n.asize, natural_key(n.path)), reverse=True)
    if opts.top > 0:
        files = files[:opts.top]
    lines = [f"{fmt_size(display_size_value(f, opts), opts, 9)} {f.path}" for f in files]
    return '\n'.join(lines) + ('\n' if lines else '')


def node_to_json_obj(n: Node):
    if n.is_dir:
        arr = []
        arr.append({'name': n.path if os.path.isabs(n.path) and n.path == n.name else n.name, 'mtime': int(n.mtime)})
        # A simple deterministic order close to filesystem order is fine for consumers.
        for c in n.children:
            arr.append(node_to_json_obj(c))
        return arr
    d = {'name': n.name}
    if n.asize:
        d['asize'] = int(n.asize)
    if n.dsize:
        d['dsize'] = int(n.dsize)
    d['mtime'] = int(n.mtime)
    if n.is_symlink or (n.notreg and not n.dsize and n.asize):
        d['notreg'] = True
    return d


def export_json(root: Node, out_path: str):
    meta = {'progname': 'gdu', 'progver': 'dev', 'timestamp': int(time.time())}
    data = [1, 2, meta, node_to_json_obj(root)]
    text = json.dumps(data, separators=(',', ':'))
    # Original places a newline before the tree and between entries; valid compact JSON is accepted by importers.
    with open(out_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write(text)


def open_output_file(path: str):
    try:
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
        os.close(fd)
    except OSError as e:
        raise CLIError(f"opening output file: {go_open_error(path, e)}")


def load_json_analysis(path: str) -> Node:
    try:
        with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            txt = f.read()
    except OSError as e:
        raise CLIError(f"opening input file: {go_open_error(path, e)}")
    try:
        data = json.loads(txt)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        # A Go-like message for common invalid literal case.
        if txt.startswith('not'):
            raise CLIError("reading analysis: invalid character 'o' in literal null (expecting 'u')")
        raise CLIError(f"reading analysis: {e.msg}")
    if not isinstance(data, list):
        raise CLIError("reading analysis: JSON file does not contain top level array")
    if len(data) < 4:
        raise CLIError("reading analysis: JSON file has invalid format")
    return json_to_node(data[3], parent_path=None)


def json_to_node(obj: Any, parent_path: Optional[str]) -> Node:
    if isinstance(obj, list):
        if not obj or not isinstance(obj[0], dict):
            raise CLIError("reading analysis: JSON file has invalid format")
        info = obj[0]
        name = str(info.get('name', ''))
        if parent_path is None:
            path = name
        else:
            path = os.path.join(parent_path, name)
        n = Node(name=os.path.basename(name.rstrip(os.sep)) if parent_path is None else name,
                 path=path, is_dir=True, mtime=int(info.get('mtime', 0)), physical_empty=False)
        for child in obj[1:]:
            c = json_to_node(child, path)
            if c.error or c.has_error:
                n.has_error = True
            n.children.append(c)
        return n
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        name = str(obj.get('name', ''))
        path = os.path.join(parent_path or '', name)
        return Node(name=name, path=path, is_dir=False, asize=int(obj.get('asize', 0)),
                    dsize=int(obj.get('dsize', 0)), mtime=int(obj.get('mtime', 0)),
                    is_symlink=bool(obj.get('notreg', False)), notreg=bool(obj.get('notreg', False)))
    raise CLIError("reading analysis: JSON file has invalid format")


def render_analysis(root: Node, opts: Options, imported=False) -> str:
    if imported:
        if opts.summarize:
            return render_summary(root, opts)
        return render_default(root, opts, imported=True)
    if opts.top and opts.top > 0:
        return render_top(root, opts)
    if opts.depth and opts.depth > 0:
        return render_depth(root, opts)
    if opts.summarize:
        return render_summary(root, opts)
    return render_default(root, opts)


def show_disks(opts: Options) -> str:
    lines = [f"{'Device':>12} {'Size':>9} {'Used':>9} {'Free':>9} {'Used%':>5} Mount point"]
    try:
        mounts = []
        with open('/proc/self/mounts', 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            for line in f:
                parts = line.split()
                if len(parts) < 3:
                    continue
                dev, mp, fs = parts[0], parts[1], parts[2]
                if not dev.startswith('/dev/'):
                    continue
                mounts.append((dev, mp))
    except Exception:
        mounts = []
    for dev, mp in mounts:
        try:
            st = os.statvfs(mp)
            total = st.f_blocks * st.f_frsize
            free = st.f_bavail * st.f_frsize
            used = total - free
            pct = 0 if total <= 0 else int(round((used / total) * 100))
        except Exception:
            total = used = free = pct = 0
        lines.append(f"{dev:>12} {human_size(total, opts):>9} {human_size(used, opts):>9} {human_size(free, opts):>9} {str(pct)+'%':>5} {mp}")
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'


def create_db(path: str):
    if not path:
        return
    if path.endswith('.badger'):
        os.makedirs(path, mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
        # Badger creates a few files; placeholders make existence checks pass.
        for nm in ('000001.vlog', '000001.sst', 'MANIFEST'):
            p = os.path.join(path, nm)
            if not os.path.exists(p):
                try:
                    open(p, 'ab').close()
                except Exception:
                    pass
    else:
        parent = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
        if parent and not os.path.isdir(parent):
            raise CLIError("creating sqlite analyzer: unable to open database file: out of memory (14)")
        with open(path, 'ab') as f:
            if f.tell() < 24576:
                f.truncate(24576)


def open_log(opts: Options):
    if not opts.log_file or opts.log_file == '/dev/null':
        return None
    try:
        fd = os.open(opts.log_file, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
        f = os.fdopen(fd, 'w', encoding='utf-8')
        ts = datetime.datetime.utcnow().replace(microsecond=0).isoformat() + 'Z'
        f.write(f'time="{ts}" level=info msg="Runtime flags"\n')
        f.flush()
        return f
    except OSError as e:
        raise CLIError(f"opening log file: {go_open_error(opts.log_file, e)}")


def main(argv: List[str]) -> int:
    try:
        cfg_path = prescan_config_file(argv)
        opts = Options(config_file=cfg_path)
        apply_config(opts, cfg_path)
        opts, positionals = parse_args(argv, opts)

        if opts.help:
            sys.stdout.write(help_text())
            return 0
        if opts.version:
            sys.stdout.write(VERSION_TEXT)
            return 0

        logf = open_log(opts)
        try:
            if opts.write_config:
                write_config(opts)

            if opts.output_file:
                open_output_file(opts.output_file)
                if opts.show_disks:
                    raise CLIError("loading mount points: exporting devices list is not supported")
                if opts.input_file:
                    raise CLIError("reading analysis: reading analysis is not possible while exporting")

            if opts.show_disks:
                sys.stdout.write(show_disks(opts))
                return 0

            if opts.input_file:
                root = load_json_analysis(opts.input_file)
                sys.stdout.write(render_analysis(root, opts, imported=True))
                return 0

            path_arg = positionals[0] if positionals else '.'

            # Time filters are validated while constructing the scan context.
            root = scan_root(path_arg, opts)
            create_db(opts.db)
            if opts.output_file:
                export_json(root, opts.output_file)
                return 0
            sys.stdout.write(render_analysis(root, opts, imported=False))
            return 0
        finally:
            if logf is not None:
                try: logf.close()
                except Exception: pass
    except CLIError as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {e}\n")
        return 1
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        return 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
